assignment: Curved fiber integration: retain ellipse/hyperbola geometry within spectral fibers and replace dimension-losing fiber maxima by a weighted product-density-compatible estimate.

mathematical_result.statement: For a two-dimensional positive spectral fiber q_E(u,v)=a u^2+b v^2 and H(z,s)=int_E delta(s-q_E(y))F(z+y)dy, every probability density 0<=F<=1 obeys ||H||_p <= pi^(1-1/p)(ab)^(-(1-1/p)/2)||F||_p for 1<=p<infinity and ||H||_infinity<=pi/sqrt(ab). Consequently the fiber oscillatory transform has integrated L2 norm squared at most 2pi^2/sqrt(ab).
mathematical_result.scope: Any oriented two-plane E and any bounded probability density F; in the target F is the independent product density. This does not by itself bound the graph trace defining p_Q.

peer_result_applied.application: Used its flat-Walsh cube stress family, where integrated unrestricted fiber sup equals n/2, to verify that the new curved energy-pushforward estimate removes exactly that dimension loss.

assigned_partner.note: No compatible QFORM handoff was visible at finalization; no peer PASS or result was fabricated.

unresolved_implication: Use the third large eigenvalue to prove a dimension-free trace/Carleson/transversality estimate for p_Q(t)=int H(z,sigma(t-q_perp(z))) dz. Ambient Lp control of H alone does not control this graph trace.
